edgeCases: New goal created with no assigned employees — Goals Listing shows '0' for department-assigned and '0' for organization-assigned counts.
Goal with zero department-assigned and zero organization-assigned employees is removed entirely from the database.
Goal has zero employees assigned within the user's own department but is used by employees of other departments — Delete option is disabled even though the count is 0 for the user's department.
Goal is assigned to at least one employee (any department) — Delete option is disabled and deletion is blocked entirely.
User with access to multiple departments toggles the per-goal department filter to view only one selected department's employees for that goal.
Fuzzy search for Goal Name returns an existing goal with a very similar (not identical) name — the duplicate-goal warning popup must appear before allowing creation of a new goal.

Goal Type is switched between Technical and Certificate before saving a new goal — Certificate Code field visibility/enablement toggles accordingly; retention of a previously entered Certificate Code value on switching back is unspecified.
RM views a goal's employee list — only members of their own team are visible, even if the goal's total organization-level assigned count is higher.
TM/EM views a goal's employee list — only employees belonging to their own managed department(s) are visible.
Multiple goals have an identical number of allocated employees — sort order/stability for tied counts is unspecified.

TM/EM/Admin edits the Assigned Employees list on an existing goal — the employee list offered is scoped to the current editor's access, which may differ from the scope of whoever originally created the goal.
Assign to field on Add Goal is limited to employees the creating user has access to — an RM cannot select employees outside their own team.
Employee counts shown for a goal (department-assigned, organization-assigned, and the sort-driving allocated count) must always reconcile with each other and with the underlying API response.
Any destructive action on a goal (deletion, or the automatic DB-level removal of a zero-assignment goal) should be preceded by a confirmation step before executing.
After any create, edit, assign, or delete operation on a goal, the Goals Listing and any open Employee Details modal / Goals tab must reflect the change immediately without a full page reload.
Goals must remain sorted by descending allocated-employee count after every assignment/unassignment or deletion, without the user manually re-triggering the sort.
Row-level Edit and Delete controls for a goal must remain present and correctly reflect the current assignment state immediately after any create, edit, assign, or delete operation.

Goals relocated again (2026-09-22): /employee/goals is a live route once more and now hosts a three-tab sub-app — Dashboard, Employee Goals, Goal Management. The old single Goals listing is now only the Goal Management tab.

Landing on /employee/goals with no query string self-redirects to ?departmentId=<the signed-in user own department> — the id differs per user (MANAGEMENT for the CEO, the TM own department for the TM).

The Dashboard tab does not hydrate its Department picker from the departmentId already in its own URL: picker reads "Select department" and the empty state renders, while the Goal Management tab on the same screen DOES honour the same id.
The tab query param is written on tab click (tab=employee-goals, tab=management) but never read on load — every deep link opens on Dashboard.
Each of the three tabs keeps its own independent department selection; choosing a department on Dashboard leaves Employee Goals on "All Departments" and Goal Management on its own value.
Total L&D Hours on the Dashboard does not respond to the Year filter, while Employees with Goals and Total Goal Assignments do.
The Year filter is not represented in the URL, so a year-filtered dashboard cannot be shared and reverts on reload.
Employee Goals renders every employee row at once (3,648 rows for an Admin) with no pagination, no page-size control and no virtualisation; first row paints after ~16.6s.
Goal Management advertises "Showing 1 - 100 of 426 results" but has no pagination control — 326 goals are reachable only via search.
Goal Management sorts the Goal Name column on the stored name while rendering the certificate-code-prefixed label, so certificate goals appear out of order to the user.
The Goal Name column filter lists raw goal names while the table cells show the certificate-prefixed form, so the two lists cannot be matched by eye.
Employees with zero assigned goals still report non-zero L&D Hours on the Employee Goals tab.
The Progress History column reads "No progress recorded" even for goals with a non-zero completion percentage and a start date.
The Employee Goals row expander is a bare <td> with an sr-only label and an icon — no role, no tabindex, no aria-expanded, so it is unreachable by keyboard.
Assigned Emp. (Dept.) mixes "None" and numeric "0" as its empty representation within one column.

Dashboard KPI/chart data is assembled client-side: the Admin landing walks GET /employees pages 1-13 at limit=300 and a department selection walks GET /employee-goals pages 1-14 at limit=300 with includeHistory=true.
On a 375px viewport the Goal Management tab label is clipped off the right edge of the tab strip and the Goal Tracking Health donut overflows its card.
Terminology for the same concept varies within one screen: "Overdue Goals" (column), "Delayed" (status filter and badge) and "At-Risk (Delayed)" (dashboard card).

The Add/Edit Goal panel gained four rich-text editors (Description, Learning Objectives, Definition of Done, Topics & Concepts) and an Estimated Duration triple (Months/Weeks/Days, min=0, no max, no step).
Goal Name input carries no maxlength attribute, and renders in its red invalid state the instant the Add Goal panel opens, before any user interaction.

There is no UI anywhere in this build to assign a goal to an employee or record progress — the Employee Goals expansion is entirely read-only and the Assign-to field is still absent from the Add/Edit panel.

6.3.x (2026-10-07): Goals is a 2-tab screen — Dashboard (default) and Goals (?tab=goals) with inner tablist 'Goals view': By Employee (default) / By Goal (&view=catalog). Shared 'Goal filters' group (Year, Department, RM [Admin only], Timeframe default 'Last 15 days') persists across tab switches; deep links ?tab=/view= are honoured; unknown tab falls back to Dashboard.

Timeframe only changes the L&D Hours / Billable Hours KPI tiles (Admin: 5d 70,504h, 15d 157,867h, All time 3,728,944h); Total Employees, Employees with Goals and Goal Assignments do not change with Timeframe. timeFrame and departmentId are written to the URL.

TM now has a Department picker defaulting to 'All Departments', but its options are only the TM's managed departments (ANDROID, CSM, QA) and All Departments = their union (279), not org-wide; foreign departmentId via URL or API returns 0 rows. PM has no Department picker; RM filter is Admin-only.
PMO 'Your Team Goal Status' caption showed 3,644 employees while the Total Employees KPI showed 3,648 (2026-10-07).

By Employee is server-paged (100/page, 'Showing 1 - 100 of 3648 results', 37 pages); the row itself is the expander (tabindex=0, aria-expanded, 'Show goals'/'Hide goals'); expansion has an Actions column 'Edit goal <name>' that opens the goal-definition Edit Goal dialog — still no assign/progress UI.
Expansion Start/End Date still render '—' and Progress History still reads 'No progress recorded' for an In Progress 20% goal, despite the 6.3.0 'Not specified' convention.

By Goal: Description cells render blank or the literal text 'undefined' (e.g. TC049-1784178347632) for goals without a description; unassigned goals show 'None' in both Assigned columns; Delete is enabled only when Org count is None.

Numeric column filters on By Employee are an unnamed popover dialog with sliders 'Minimum'/'Maximum' and Clear/Save; 'Table options' is also an unnamed dialog (list 'Column Visibility' with switches + 'Drag to reorder').

API /employee-goals/dashboard, /filter-options and /employee-goals/employees return 200 with empty data to Employee and CSM tokens (not 403); /employee-goals returns only the caller's own assignments for Employee; /goals is 403 for both. List endpoints reject limit values other than 100, 200, 300 with 400.
Browser Back after switching Goals tabs still lands on about:blank, and closing Add Goal with Escape still drops focus to <body> (6.3.2).
businessRules: Employee counts shown for a goal (department-assigned count, organization-assigned count, and the count driving Goals Listing sort order) must always reconcile with each other and with the underlying API response.

Any goal/assignment data written via the Add Goal side panel or the edit-goal flow (Description, Certificate Code, Assigned Employees) must be retrievable via the corresponding API with identical values.
Clicking Save on the Add Goal side panel twice in quick succession must not create duplicate goal records.

Each role's permitted and forbidden goal actions (create, assign, edit, delete) must be enforced at both UI level (control hidden/disabled) and API level (403 on unauthorized write), not merely restricted in the UI.
Any destructive action on a goal (deletion, and the DB-level auto-removal of a zero-assignment goal) must be preceded by a confirmation step before executing.

After any create, edit, assign, or delete operation on a goal, the Goals Listing and any open Employee Details modal / Goals tab must reflect the change immediately, without requiring a full page reload.
Goals must remain sorted by descending allocated-employee count after every assignment/unassignment or deletion; re-sorting must occur without requiring the user to manually re-trigger the sort.

The row-level Edit and Delete controls for a goal must remain present and correctly reflect the current assignment state immediately after any create, edit, assign, or delete operation — not disappear or fail to update the enabled/disabled state without a page reload.

Once a goal is created, only Certificate Code and Description remain editable via the Edit action — all other fields (Goal Name, Goal Type, etc.) are locked/read-only (manual requirement, 2026-08-19).

The Goals Listing shows two distinct employee-count columns per goal: a department-scoped assigned count (reacts to the current department filter) and an organization-level total assigned count (constant regardless of filter) — the two must never be conflated (manual requirement, 2026-08-19).

Goals access is role-gated: the base Employee and CSM personas are redirected to /unauthorized and get no Goals sidebar link; Admin, TM and PM get the full three-tab screen (verified live 2026-09-22).

Department-scoped roles (TM, PM) get no department picker and their scope cannot be widened by injecting a foreign departmentId into the URL — verified live 2026-09-22, KPIs were identical with and without the injected id. Permanent regression guard.
Goal Type drives Certificate Code: the field is present only for Certificate goals and Save stays disabled for a Certificate goal until a code is supplied.
Edit Goal locks Goal Name and Goal Type (rendered disabled); Description, Learning Objectives, Definition of Done, Topics & Concepts and Estimated Duration remain editable.

Delete keys on the organisation-level assigned count, not the department-scoped one: every goal with a non-zero organisation count has Delete disabled, including those showing None/0 for the current department.
Save on the Add Goal panel is disabled until the mandatory fields are valid, and Save on the Edit panel is disabled until a value actually changes.
Employees with Goals must never exceed Total Employees, and the Employee Goal Coverage donut must split exactly into those two figures.
The per-goal organisation breakdown popover must sum to the Assigned Emp. (Org.) figure on the same row, and its entry for the active department must equal Assigned Emp. (Dept.).
A parent row Goals count on the Employee Goals tab must equal the number of rows in its expansion, and Overdue Goals must equal the Delayed rows within it.
